nodes.title: The G2 browser gate's leak.key_position check (server/forge/g2/qa.js) failed a correct game by chance. The kit re-shuffles options with crypto randomness on every mount, and one play failed if the key sat at the same option index on all items; on a topic with 4,4,4,4,2 options that happens about once in 256 plays with nothing wrong. In tests/forge-g2-browser it surfaced as 'the scripted builder ran out of responses' (once in integration 38's test:all); in production it would send the builder back to the model for a paid round. Reproduced by an agent: 1 failure in about 365 gate runs, no effect of CPU load (0 in 18 runs under 4 to 16 busy loops alone); forcing a constant position reproduces the exact error. Fixed: the gate plays twice already, and now fails only when the key is constant within each of the two plays (about 1 in 65,536 by chance), whether or not the two plays agree on the index, so a mechanic that pins the key to one slot per mount is still caught. Not proven: that the one failure seen in test:all was this check (the output did not record which check failed). Also noted, not seen firing: a 50 ms wall-clock Budget.slow_call in the kit runtime.

Rejected as a habit: pushing an integration on 'the failing suite passes alone and the diff does not touch it'. Used three times on 2026-11-10 and 11 (integrations 32, 37, 38). Each time the cause, once found, was specific and not load: a wall-clock assertion, a test assumption broken by another stream's data, a 1-in-256 chance failure in a product gate. The pushes did no harm, but the reasoning given at the time ('load') was wrong in every case that was later explained. A failure that passes alone gets a root-cause task the same hour, and the push message says 'cause unknown' rather than naming one.
